subject.title: [Bug]: Compaction fails with 'Thread group size (1024) exceeds maximum threads per threadgroup (896)'

question: Should failed overflow compaction for OpenAI-compatible local providers continue to block with manual reset/new guidance, persist only a recoverable marker, or add a stronger provider-agnostic degraded recovery path?
rationale: Current source intentionally blocks after recovery is exhausted, while changing it affects replay safety, session continuity, local-provider behavior, and whether a new config surface is acceptable.

options.title: Design provider-agnostic recovery
options.body: Add a safe degraded recovery path or operator-visible recovery flow for compaction-provider errors without introducing an MLX-specific knob first.

options.title: Accept marker-first observability
options.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/102178 as the first supported step and leave manual reset/new recovery in place for now.

options.title: Add MLX request tuning
options.body: Add a narrow parameter only after confirming the MLX server accepts a stable request-body field that existing `extra_body` cannot express.

recommendation.title: Design provider-agnostic recovery
recommendation.body: Add a safe degraded recovery path or operator-visible recovery flow for compaction-provider errors without introducing an MLX-specific knob first.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is centered on compaction/context recovery semantics, and CONTRIBUTING.md identifies this person as the compaction and context owner.
